stem: What is the main difference between a task and an event?

options.text: An event has a start and end time on a calendar, a task has a due date
A task has a start and end time, and an event only has a due date
There is no difference, because both appear in the same list
Only events can recur, and tasks always happen once

explanation: Events are time blocks on a calendar. Tasks are to-dos with due dates and statuses.

stem: A site visit is booked for Thursday at 10:00. Which activity type should be used?

options.text: Event
Task
Case
Campaign

explanation: Anything with a fixed time slot is an event.

stem: A rep wants a reminder to send a quote by Friday. Which activity type fits?

options.text: Task
Event
Lead
Case

explanation: Tasks track to-dos with due dates and a status.

stem: Which activity type can span several days, such as a conference?

options.text: Event
Task
Both equally
Neither

explanation: Multi-day events span several days. Tasks cannot be multi-day.

stem: What does the Name (Who) field on an activity relate to?

options.text: A lead or contact
An opportunity
An account
A case

explanation: Name (Who) points to a lead or contact. Related To (What) points to records such as an account or opportunity.

stem: What can the Related To (What) field relate to?

options.text: An account, opportunity, case, campaign or custom object
Only a lead, because activities cannot relate to business records
Only a contact, which is the same as the Name field
Only a user, who owns the activity

explanation: Related To links the activity to the business record it concerns.

stem: Which feature lets an event include several contacts?

options.text: Shared activities
Recurring events
Public calendars
Macros

explanation: Shared Activities lets multiple contacts be related to one activity so it appears on each timeline.

stem: A weekly Monday meeting should repeat. Which feature fits?

options.text: Recurring events
Shared activities
Multi-day events
Public calendars

explanation: Recurring events repeat on a pattern, and you can edit one occurrence or the series.

stem: Which record page component shows past and upcoming activities?

options.text: Activity Timeline
Highlights panel
Path
Related list of campaigns

explanation: Activity Timeline shows upcoming and overdue items and past activity such as logged calls and emails.

stem: What does Log a Call do?

options.text: Records a call that has already happened
Schedules a future call
Starts a phone call
Creates an event on the calendar

explanation: Log a Call creates a completed task to record the conversation.

stem: Which feature lets a team share one calendar, such as site visits?

options.text: Public calendar
Private calendar
Activity Timeline
Task list

explanation: Public calendars are shared with users or groups so the team sees the same events.

stem: Which feature automatically syncs emails and events between a user's email and Salesforce?

options.text: Einstein Activity Capture
Data Loader, which imports and exports records in bulk
Web-to-Lead, which captures website form entries as leads
Campaign influence, which links campaigns to opportunities

explanation: Einstein Activity Capture syncs emails and events so reps do not have to log them manually.

stem: What do the Outlook and Gmail integrations provide?

options.text: A side panel in the email client showing Salesforce records and logging tools
A new Salesforce licence for each person who emails customers
A new profile that lets users send email from Salesforce only
A report type that shows email activity by month

explanation: The integrations show Salesforce data next to the email and help log emails and create records.

stem: What does a merge field in an email template do?

options.text: Inserts data from a record, such as the contact's name
Merges two accounts that have the same name into one record
Combines two email templates into a single longer template
Deletes the email from the sent items once it has been delivered

explanation: Merge fields pull values from records into the email.

stem: A template shows a blank name when sent. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The field on the record is empty or not accessible
The template is corrupted and needs to be rebuilt
The template needs a new letterhead before it can be sent
The user lacks a licence to send email from Salesforce

explanation: Merge fields are filled from record data, so blank fields give blank output.

stem: How should email templates be made available to a team?

options.text: Store them in a folder and share the folder
Email them to everyone on the team as attachments
Create a profile that contains all of the templates
Make them private so each person keeps their own copy

explanation: Templates are stored in folders, and folder sharing controls who can use them.

stem: What does a letterhead add to an email template?

options.text: Branding such as a logo and colours
A merge field that inserts the contact's name
A validation rule that checks the template text
An attachment limit for each email that is sent

explanation: A letterhead stores header and footer design for consistent branding.

stem: Managers cannot see what the team has done with a customer. What is the best way to make logging easy?

options.text: Use email integration, Einstein Activity Capture and quick actions
Ask reps to log every call and email by hand in a custom object
Hide the activity timeline so managers use reports only
Stop recording calls so there is nothing to track

explanation: Automating capture beats relying on reps remembering to log, and increases the quality of the history.

stem: An event can include up to how many related contacts when shared activities is on?

options.text: Unlimited

explanation: Shared activities allows an event to relate to up to 50 contacts.

stem: Which statement about tasks is true?

options.text: Tasks have a status such as Not Started or Completed
Tasks have a start and end time on a calendar
Tasks cannot be recurring
Tasks cannot be linked to contacts

explanation: Tasks have a status and a due date. They can recur and relate to records.
